provenance.network_input: simulated network and fixed candidate trips; not real supply contracts
provenance.weather_input: user planning assumption; not an observed weather value or fetched forecast
provenance.cargo_input: simulated current cargo temperature; not physical sensor telemetry
provenance.travel_input: fixed origin-destination planning duration, including already recorded simulated delays; no new road routing
provenance.model_performance: No prospective delay or cargo-failure skill is established here. Saved FSIS sampling model evaluation remains a separate scientific task.

temperature.provenance: simulated cargo-temperature scenario projection; not observed sensor data or a validated failure-risk model
assumptions: First-order thermal response; fault time constant 120 minutes, normal control 20 minutes
Normal assumed control equilibrium 2°C, with a small uncalibrated ambient penalty above 30°C
4°C is a conservative demonstration review threshold, not a lot disposition rule
Bands are parameter-sensitivity ranges, not statistical confidence intervals
No pathogen growth, consumer illness probability or automatic hold decision

exclusion_reasons: not selected under joint demand, stock, capacity and cost constraints

takeaways: Under these assumptions, scenario A selects 13 of 24 candidate trips and allocates 5,200 kg; 2,300 kg of simulated demand remains unmet.
Compared with the current inputs, these chosen delay/fault assumptions change scenario-A unmet demand by +0 kg. This is an observed planning comparison, not a learned forecast.
2 candidate trips exceed their relative delivery deadlines. Candidate checks include trips that may never be selected.
2 candidates have a modeled temperature above the 4°C demonstration review level during their checked window, capped at six hours. Review flags do not create holds.
limitations: This is a relative one-wave simulation with a six-hour thermal check horizon, not today's dispatch schedule, a live ETA or a learned forecast.
Added delay is applied uniformly to every candidate as an explicit planning assumption; it is not estimated from road closures or weather.
Thermal coefficients are uncalibrated. A projected value above the 4°C demonstration review level is not a regulatory finding, pathogen-growth estimate or consumer-illness probability.
Projected temperatures flag candidates for review only. They do not replace current cargo readings, create holds, or enter scenario C as newly observed excursions.
Scenario C holds remain proposed until separate human approval. Held, recalled and ineligible stock stays excluded under every allocation.
Scenario D can substitute eligible simulated lots on fixed trips; no route geometry, stop order or truck assignment is redesigned here.
Candidate counts include trips that may never be selected. Shared stock, capacity, demand, deadlines and eligibility are checked jointly by the actual allocation solver.
Baseline means a newly computed scenario-A allocation of the current inputs, not the current approved driver-assignment list.
Unmet demand and stock are one-wave quantities, not a rolling inventory ledger. Unsent stock is not automatically food waste.
Changed allocations are observed solver comparisons, not a causal proof of why one particular trip was selected.
No event, proposal, assignment, source refresh, model training or approval is performed by this calculation.
